prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: COc1cc2ncnc(Oc3ccc(F)c(Cl)c3)c2cc1OC
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL279

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of recombinant human VEGFR-2-mediated poly(Glu4Tyr) phosphorylation after 1 hr
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of recombinant human VEGFR-2 using poly(Glu4/Tyr) and [gamma32P]ATP as substrate after 1 hr by scintillation counting
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.92, "error_class": "none", "reason": "Both assays measure IC50 for inhibition of recombinant human VEGFR-2 using the same poly(Glu4Tyr) substrate, same 1-hour incubation, same organism, same assay type (binding/functional), and same confidence score, with the only difference being that Assay B specifies the radiolabeled ATP and scintillation counting readout, which is a standard kinase assay detection method fully consistent with Assay A."}
